newsitem.title: USA: Diametrics cuts U.S. workforce by 8 pct.
newsitem.headline: Diametrics cuts U.S. workforce by 8 pct.

text.p: Diametrics Medical Inc, which reported a 1997 first quarter loss of $5.8 million, said Thursday it cut the U.S. workforce in its manufacturing and development operations by 12 people or eight percent.

"This reduction is the result of our continued progress in more effectively deploying our resources and was made possible by process improvements which led to the consolidation of management and functional positions in the organization," said David Giddings, chairman and chief executive officer, in a statement.

Earlier today, the company reported a 1997 first quarter net loss of $5.8 million or $0.38 per share, compared with a net loss of $5.5 million or $0.37 for the same quarter last year. Sales rose 220 percent to a record $1.95 million from $609,571 for the same period last year.

Diametrics said its 1997 first quarter sales exceeded sales for the 1996 fourth quarter, reflecting new products acquired in its purchase of the Biomedical Sensors Ltd unit from Pfizer Inc in November 1996.

Giddings said the company continues to look for strategic alliances in the diagnostics, critical care and pharmaceutical industries. In the first quarter, Diametrics formed an alliance with Marquette Medical Systems Inc to develop an interface that links the technology of both companies. The interface is expected to be launched this year.

Diametrics also said it plans to introduce in the third quarter of 1997, a new product which offers tests for blood gases, electrolytes and hematocrit on one cartridge. The company said the addition of this combination cartridge will make its IRMA SL system more cost effective for use in high volume testing.
